scr_ar_editing_customer_contact_informat.purpose: Overview of editing the bill-to or ship-to contact directly from an A/R invoice or adjustment rather than from the customer master record.
scr_ar_editing_customer_contact_informat.outcome: A single invoice goes to the right person without changing the customer's defaults.
scr_ar_editing_customer_contact_informat.rootCause: Commercial tenants sometimes need a one-off invoice routed elsewhere (a lender-required escrow contact, a new AP clerk); editing at transaction level handles the exception without corrupting the master contact.
scr_ar_editing_customer_contact_informat.ifSkipped: Users overwrite master contacts for one-off needs and later invoices go to the wrong person.
redFlags: Master contacts changed to fix a single invoice

scr_ar_editing_contact_information_from_.purpose: Edits the contact details on an A/R invoice while it is being created, with the option to save the change back to the contact record or keep it transaction-only.
scr_ar_editing_contact_information_from_.outcome: The invoice carries the correct billing contact from the start.
scr_ar_editing_contact_information_from_.rootCause: Choosing whether a contact edit is permanent or one-off at creation time is what keeps the contact master accurate while still handling exceptions.
scr_ar_editing_contact_information_from_.ifSkipped: Temporary contact changes become permanent and misroute future invoices.
redFlags: Contact edits saved to master without verification

scr_ar_editing_contact_information_in_an.purpose: Edits the contact on an existing A/R invoice — for example after a tenant reports the invoice went to a former employee — before re-sending it.
scr_ar_editing_contact_information_in_an.outcome: A misdirected invoice corrected and re-sent to the right contact.
scr_ar_editing_contact_information_in_an.rootCause: Undelivered invoices age without the customer knowing they exist; correcting the contact and re-sending restarts the collection clock with a valid delivery.
scr_ar_editing_contact_information_in_an.ifSkipped: The customer never receives the invoice and it ages into a write-off.
redFlags: Invoices re-sent without updating the master contact

scr_ar_changing_to_a_different_contact_i.purpose: Switches an existing A/R invoice to a different stored contact — for example from the tenant's site manager to their corporate AP department.
scr_ar_changing_to_a_different_contact_i.outcome: The invoice is routed to the contact that actually pays.
scr_ar_changing_to_a_different_contact_i.rootCause: National tenants pay through central AP; invoices addressed to local store managers stall, so selecting the right stored contact speeds payment.
scr_ar_changing_to_a_different_contact_i.ifSkipped: Invoices stall with contacts who cannot approve payment.
redFlags: National tenants billed at store level

scr_ar_using_the_multi_select_box.purpose: Explains the multi-select box used on A/R setup and report pages to pick several entities, customers or accounts at once.
scr_ar_using_the_multi_select_box.outcome: Batch selections made accurately across many properties.
scr_ar_using_the_multi_select_box.rootCause: Portfolio-level runs (statements, aging, permissions) depend on selecting the right set of entities; misusing multi-select silently omits properties from the run.
scr_ar_using_the_multi_select_box.ifSkipped: Properties are left out of batch runs without anyone noticing.
redFlags: Batch runs covering fewer entities than the portfolio list

scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_safar.purpose: Browser-specific steps for printing RealPage A/R PDFs (invoices, statements) from Safari without scaling or blank-page problems.
scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_safar.outcome: Printed invoices and statements that are complete and legible.
scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_safar.rootCause: Mailed statements and invoices must print at full page with remittance stubs intact; browser PDF settings can crop or scale them, causing payment processing issues at lockbox.
scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_safar.ifSkipped: Printed invoices are cropped and remittance stubs cannot be read at the lockbox.
redFlags: Remittance stubs cut off

scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_firef.purpose: Firefox-specific steps for printing A/R PDFs, particularly turning off 'fit to page' so invoice and statement layouts print at true size.
scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_firef.outcome: Correctly scaled invoice and statement printouts from Firefox.
scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_firef.rootCause: Firefox's built-in PDF viewer can shrink documents to fit; scaled remittance slips and window-envelope addresses then fail to align.
scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_firef.ifSkipped: Addresses miss the envelope window and mail is returned.
redFlags: Returned mail from misaligned addresses

scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_micro.purpose: Microsoft Edge-specific steps for printing A/R PDFs so invoices and statements print completely and at the right scale.
scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_micro.outcome: Reliable printing of A/R documents from Edge.
scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_micro.rootCause: Edge is the default browser on many corporate Windows builds used by onshore and offshore teams; its PDF defaults need adjusting to avoid clipped documents.
scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_micro.ifSkipped: Documents print incompletely and must be reprinted and re-mailed.
redFlags: Repeated reprints of the same batch

scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_chrom.purpose: Chrome-specific steps for printing A/R PDFs — margins, scale and pop-up settings — so invoice and statement batches print in full.
scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_chrom.outcome: Complete, correctly scaled batch printing from Chrome.
scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_chrom.rootCause: Chrome can block the pop-up that opens a batch PDF; users then believe statements printed when they did not, and customers never receive them.
scr_ar_printing_pdf_documents_from_chrom.ifSkipped: Statement batches silently fail to open and are never mailed.
redFlags: Batch print runs with no printed output

scr_ar_help_and_support.purpose: Points A/R users to RealPage help resources — online help, the client portal, downloadable guides and support tickets.
scr_ar_help_and_support.outcome: Users can find authoritative answers before improvising workarounds.
scr_ar_help_and_support.rootCause: Undocumented workarounds (manual JEs to fix an A/R issue) are a leading source of subledger-to-GL breaks; using official support first keeps fixes inside the system.
scr_ar_help_and_support.ifSkipped: Users invent workarounds that break the A/R-to-GL reconciliation.
redFlags: Manual JEs used to correct system issues

scr_ar_unified_platform_help_and_support.purpose: Help and support available inside the RealPage Unified Platform for A/R users, including in-product help and ticket submission.
scr_ar_unified_platform_help_and_support.outcome: Faster resolution of system questions from within the platform.
scr_ar_unified_platform_help_and_support.rootCause: Close deadlines leave little time for issue resolution; in-platform support shortens the time from problem to fix during month-end.
scr_ar_unified_platform_help_and_support.ifSkipped: System issues remain unresolved and delay close.
redFlags: Open support tickets blocking close tasks

scr_ar_client_portal_help.purpose: RealPage Client Portal help — knowledge base articles, release notes and case tracking relevant to A/R.
scr_ar_client_portal_help.outcome: Access to release notes and known issues affecting A/R.
scr_ar_client_portal_help.rootCause: Release changes can alter A/R behaviour (aging, penalties, statements); reading release notes prevents surprises in close results.
scr_ar_client_portal_help.ifSkipped: Release changes alter results without the team understanding why.
redFlags: Unexplained changes after a release

scr_ar_downloading_realpage_financial_su.purpose: Downloads the RealPage Financial Suite user guides (A/R, A/P, GL) as PDFs for training and offline reference.
scr_ar_downloading_realpage_financial_su.outcome: Current official procedures available for training and SOPs.
scr_ar_downloading_realpage_financial_su.rootCause: Offshore SOPs should reference the vendor's current guide so procedures stay aligned with how the software actually works after each release.
scr_ar_downloading_realpage_financial_su.ifSkipped: SOPs drift from system behaviour and training is outdated.
redFlags: SOPs citing outdated guide versions

scr_ar_how_to_read_paths.purpose: Explains how navigation paths in the guides (e.g., 'Accounts Receivable > All > Invoices') map to menus in the application.
scr_ar_how_to_read_paths.outcome: Users can follow documented procedures to the right screen.
scr_ar_how_to_read_paths.rootCause: Offshore teams follow written SOPs; misreading a path leads to performing a task on the wrong screen, such as a setup page instead of a transaction page.
scr_ar_how_to_read_paths.ifSkipped: Procedures are performed on the wrong screen.
redFlags: New staff unable to locate screens from SOPs

scr_ar_support_and_error_ids.purpose: Explains the support and error IDs shown on error messages and how to include them in support tickets for faster diagnosis.
scr_ar_support_and_error_ids.outcome: Support tickets resolved faster with precise error references.
scr_ar_support_and_error_ids.rootCause: Without the error ID, support cannot locate the failed operation in logs; A/R posting errors during close then take days instead of hours to resolve.
scr_ar_support_and_error_ids.ifSkipped: Posting errors take much longer to resolve and delay close.
redFlags: Tickets opened without error IDs

scr_ar_appendices.purpose: A/R guide appendices with reference material — field definitions and data templates for customers and invoices.
scr_ar_appendices.outcome: Field-level reference available for imports and exports.
scr_ar_appendices.rootCause: Imports and integrations need exact field definitions; appendices are the authoritative source that prevents field-mapping mistakes.
scr_ar_appendices.ifSkipped: Field mappings are guessed and data loads incorrectly.
redFlags: Integrations built without field references

scr_ar_customer_data_appendix.purpose: Appendix defining customer data fields — ID, name, type, terms, credit limit, contacts, default accounts — used in customer imports.
scr_ar_customer_data_appendix.outcome: Customer data prepared with correct field meaning and format.
scr_ar_customer_data_appendix.rootCause: Customer fields drive billing behaviour (terms, credit limits, tax); misunderstanding them during import creates systematic billing errors for every affected customer.
scr_ar_customer_data_appendix.ifSkipped: Customers are imported with wrong terms or types and billing is off.
redFlags: Imported customers with blank terms

scr_ar_customer_fields_required_for_impo.purpose: Lists the mandatory fields for importing customer records — without which the row is rejected — and their accepted formats.
scr_ar_customer_fields_required_for_impo.outcome: Customer import files pass validation on the first attempt.
scr_ar_customer_fields_required_for_impo.rootCause: Rejected customer rows block all dependent invoice rows; getting required fields right first protects the whole A/R conversion sequence.
scr_ar_customer_fields_required_for_impo.ifSkipped: Customer rows fail and every invoice for them fails too.
redFlags: High rejection rate on customer imports

scr_ar_customers_data_template.purpose: The customers data template, including how the customer ID column behaves when automatic customer numbering is enabled in A/R configuration.
scr_ar_customers_data_template.outcome: Customer templates filled in consistent with numbering settings.
scr_ar_customers_data_template.rootCause: Supplying IDs when auto-numbering is on (or omitting them when it is off) causes rejected rows or mismatched IDs, breaking the link to the seller's tenant references.
scr_ar_customers_data_template.ifSkipped: Customer IDs do not match legacy references and history cannot be traced.
redFlags: No crosswalk from legacy IDs to new IDs

scr_ar_a_r_invoice_data_appendix.purpose: Appendix defining A/R invoice data fields — customer, dates, terms, lines, account labels, amounts — for imports and integrations.
scr_ar_a_r_invoice_data_appendix.outcome: Invoice data prepared with the right fields for open-invoice loads.
scr_ar_a_r_invoice_data_appendix.rootCause: Open-invoice conversion is how the acquired aging enters the system; field errors (wrong due date or label) distort both aging buckets and revenue coding.
scr_ar_a_r_invoice_data_appendix.ifSkipped: Converted invoices land in the wrong aging buckets or revenue accounts.
redFlags: Due dates set equal to conversion date

scr_ar_a_r_invoice_data.purpose: Detailed invoice data definitions and how to export existing invoice data as a model for preparing import files.
scr_ar_a_r_invoice_data.outcome: Invoice import files that match the system's own export format.
scr_ar_a_r_invoice_data.rootCause: Exporting a known-good invoice and mirroring its format is the most reliable way to avoid field-format mistakes in bulk loads.
scr_ar_a_r_invoice_data.ifSkipped: Import files are built from scratch with format errors.
redFlags: Date formats differing from export

scr_ar_configuring_accounts_receivable.purpose: Chapter on configuring Accounts Receivable end to end — summaries, thresholds, discounts, intercompany billing, bank accounts, dimensions, aging, formatting and PEX.
scr_ar_configuring_accounts_receivable.outcome: A/R set up once, coherently, to match accounting policy.
scr_ar_configuring_accounts_receivable.rootCause: A/R configuration determines how every invoice and receipt posts, ages and prints; a coherent configuration pass at implementation prevents years of workaround entries.
scr_ar_configuring_accounts_receivable.ifSkipped: Piecemeal configuration leaves conflicting settings and systematic errors.
redFlags: No documented configuration baseline

scr_ar_accounts_receivable_configuration.purpose: The ordered workflow for configuring A/R — which settings come first (accounts, summaries, terms) and which depend on them (labels, templates, thresholds).
scr_ar_accounts_receivable_configuration.outcome: Configuration completed in a dependency-safe order.
scr_ar_accounts_receivable_configuration.rootCause: Some settings reference others (labels need GL accounts, bill-backs need entities); following the workflow order avoids incomplete setups that fail at first billing.
scr_ar_accounts_receivable_configuration.ifSkipped: First billing run fails due to missing dependent setup.
redFlags: Go-live with incomplete configuration checklist

scr_ar_configure_accounts_receivable_pag.purpose: The Configure Accounts Receivable page holding all A/R settings — summaries, posting accounts, numbering, thresholds, aging and formatting options.
scr_ar_configure_accounts_receivable_pag.outcome: Central control of A/R behaviour for the company.
scr_ar_configure_accounts_receivable_pag.rootCause: Every A/R setting lives here, so changes on this page affect all properties at once; access and changes must be restricted and logged.
scr_ar_configure_accounts_receivable_pag.ifSkipped: Uncontrolled changes alter A/R behaviour portfolio-wide.
redFlags: Configuration edits by non-admin users
Changes during close window

scr_ar_creating_automatic_summaries_2.purpose: Configures automatic A/R summaries (monthly or daily) so invoices and receipts are grouped by period for posting without manual summary creation.
scr_ar_creating_automatic_summaries_2.outcome: Invoices and receipts always land in a summary for the right period.
scr_ar_creating_automatic_summaries_2.rootCause: Manual summaries are a frequent source of cutoff errors when misdated; automatic summaries tie each transaction's GL period to its date.
scr_ar_creating_automatic_summaries_2.ifSkipped: Manually created summaries misdate batches and shift revenue or cash between months.
redFlags: Automatic summaries turned off

scr_ar_configuring_a_r_thresholds.purpose: Sets A/R thresholds — amounts above which invoices, adjustments or credits require approval or trigger warnings.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_thresholds.outcome: Large or unusual A/R transactions routed for review.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_thresholds.rootCause: Large credits and write-offs directly reduce revenue and NOI; thresholds ensure they are approved by someone other than the preparer.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_thresholds.ifSkipped: Large credits post without approval, a common revenue manipulation risk.
redFlags: Thresholds set so high nothing is reviewed
Credits split to stay below threshold

scr_ar_configuring_the_system_to_apply_d.purpose: Configures RealPage to apply early-payment discounts automatically when a customer pays within the discount window defined by their terms.
scr_ar_configuring_the_system_to_apply_d.outcome: Earned discounts applied consistently without manual adjustments.
scr_ar_configuring_the_system_to_apply_d.rootCause: Discounts reduce revenue; applying them automatically only when earned prevents both overcharging customers and giving unearned discounts.
scr_ar_configuring_the_system_to_apply_d.ifSkipped: Discounts are applied inconsistently and revenue is misstated.
redFlags: Discounts taken after the discount window

scr_ar_configuring_intercompany_billing.purpose: Configures intercompany billing so one entity can invoice another, creating matching receivables and payables between affiliated owners or funds.
scr_ar_configuring_intercompany_billing.outcome: Affiliate charges recorded symmetrically in both entities.
scr_ar_configuring_intercompany_billing.rootCause: Shared-service charges between entities must mirror exactly to eliminate on consolidation and to be defensible to separate ownership groups.
scr_ar_configuring_intercompany_billing.ifSkipped: Intercompany balances do not mirror and eliminations fail.
redFlags: Intercompany billing between entities with different owners without approval

scr_ar_adding_a_sequence_id.purpose: Adds a numbering sequence used for intercompany billing documents so they are uniquely numbered and distinguishable from third-party invoices.
scr_ar_adding_a_sequence_id.outcome: Intercompany invoices identifiable by their number series.
scr_ar_adding_a_sequence_id.rootCause: A separate sequence lets reviewers and consolidators isolate intercompany documents quickly and test completeness of eliminations.
scr_ar_adding_a_sequence_id.ifSkipped: Intercompany invoices mix with third-party billing and are hard to eliminate.
redFlags: Intercompany using the third-party sequence

scr_ar_configuring_intercompany_billing_.purpose: Detailed intercompany billing setup — sequence IDs, receiving-entity accounts and automatic bill creation in the billed entity.
scr_ar_configuring_intercompany_billing_.outcome: Intercompany invoices automatically create matching bills.
scr_ar_configuring_intercompany_billing_.rootCause: Automating the payable side removes the risk that the billed entity never records the charge, which is the main cause of intercompany out-of-balance.
scr_ar_configuring_intercompany_billing_.ifSkipped: Billed entities miss charges and intercompany balances diverge.
redFlags: Intercompany invoices without a matching bill

scr_ar_defining_the_default_bank_account.purpose: Defines the default bank account on an entity so A/R receipts for that property deposit to its own operating account.
scr_ar_defining_the_default_bank_account.outcome: Each property's receipts go to its own bank account.
scr_ar_defining_the_default_bank_account.rootCause: Management agreements and lender covenants require property funds to stay in property accounts; a wrong default commingles funds across owners.
scr_ar_defining_the_default_bank_account.ifSkipped: Receipts deposit to another owner's account — a commingling and fiduciary breach.
redFlags: Entities sharing a default bank account

scr_ar_configuring_a_r_screen_settings.purpose: Configures A/R screen settings — which fields show on invoice and receipt forms and their defaults.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_screen_settings.outcome: Forms show only the fields the company uses, in the right order.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_screen_settings.rootCause: Cluttered forms lead to fields being skipped or filled wrongly; tailoring them reduces keying errors on high-volume billing.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_screen_settings.ifSkipped: Users fill forms inconsistently and required data is missed.
redFlags: Important fields hidden from forms

scr_ar_configuring_a_r_dimensions.purpose: Configures which dimensions (location, department, project, customer) are required or available on A/R transactions.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_dimensions.outcome: A/R transactions carry the dimensions reporting needs.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_dimensions.rootCause: Owner and property reporting filter on location and department; if A/R lines lack them, revenue drops out of property-level P&Ls.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_dimensions.ifSkipped: Revenue is missing from property P&Ls because lines lack a location.
redFlags: A/R lines with blank location

scr_ar_configuring_a_r_aging.purpose: Configures A/R aging — bucket ranges, aging by invoice or due date, and whether reversals display as history — so the aging matches company policy.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_aging.outcome: An aging report aligned with collection and reserve policy.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_aging.rootCause: The ASC 326 reserve and collection priorities are computed from aging buckets; bucket definitions must match policy or both the reserve and delinquency reporting are wrong.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_aging.ifSkipped: Reserve calculations and delinquency reports use the wrong buckets.
redFlags: Aging basis changed mid-year

scr_ar_configuring_a_r_formatting.purpose: Configures A/R formatting — invoice and statement templates, logos, remittance addresses and messages.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_formatting.outcome: Professional documents with correct remittance instructions.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_formatting.rootCause: Remittance addresses and bank details on invoices determine where customers pay; wrong or outdated instructions misdirect payments and create fraud risk.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_formatting.ifSkipped: Customers pay to old addresses or accounts and cash is lost or delayed.
redFlags: Remittance details changed without treasury verification

scr_ar_auto_payment_suggestions.purpose: Auto payment suggestions propose how an intercompany or customer payment should be applied to open invoices, reducing manual matching.
scr_ar_auto_payment_suggestions.outcome: Payments applied to the right invoices faster.
scr_ar_auto_payment_suggestions.rootCause: Manual application of large remittances covering many invoices is error-prone; suggestions based on amounts and references reduce misapplication.
scr_ar_auto_payment_suggestions.ifSkipped: Payments are misapplied and the aging shows false delinquencies.
redFlags: Suggestions accepted without review

scr_ar_setting_up_a_default_bank_account.purpose: Sets the default bank account in A/R payment configuration used when receipts do not specify one.
scr_ar_setting_up_a_default_bank_account.outcome: Receipts without explicit bank selection deposit correctly.
scr_ar_setting_up_a_default_bank_account.rootCause: The default is used silently; pointing it to the right operating account prevents receipts from posting to a reserve or security deposit account.
scr_ar_setting_up_a_default_bank_account.ifSkipped: Receipts post to the wrong bank account and bank recs break.
redFlags: Default set to security deposit account

scr_ar_pex_configuration.purpose: Configures the PEX integration — credentials, card-to-account mapping and default coding — for importing PEX card transactions.
scr_ar_pex_configuration.outcome: PEX transactions import with correct accounts and dimensions.
scr_ar_pex_configuration.rootCause: Mapping PEX cards to properties and expense accounts is what makes imported card spend land on the right property P&L.
scr_ar_pex_configuration.ifSkipped: Card spend imports to the wrong property or account.
redFlags: Cards not mapped to a property

scr_ar_enabling_the_intercompany_bill_ba.purpose: Enables the intercompany bill-back subscription from the A/R configuration chapter, the first step in setting up automated cost recovery between entities.
scr_ar_enabling_the_intercompany_bill_ba.outcome: Bill-back capability switched on for the company.
scr_ar_enabling_the_intercompany_bill_ba.rootCause: Without the subscription enabled, bill-back templates cannot be used and staff fall back on manual intercompany entries that are harder to reconcile.
scr_ar_enabling_the_intercompany_bill_ba.ifSkipped: Shared costs are recovered via manual JEs with no audit trail between entities.
redFlags: Manual intercompany entries persisting after enablement

scr_ar_create_vendors_and_customers_for_.purpose: Creates the paired vendor and customer records per entity required for bill-backs, from the A/R configuration chapter.
scr_ar_create_vendors_and_customers_for_.outcome: Every entity has intercompany counterpart records.
scr_ar_create_vendors_and_customers_for_.rootCause: Bill-backs post a customer invoice in one entity and a vendor bill in another; both records must exist and be clearly flagged as affiliates.
scr_ar_create_vendors_and_customers_for_.ifSkipped: Bill-backs cannot be created or post against external parties.
redFlags: Affiliate vendors set up with 1099 reporting

scr_ar_setting_up_override_accounts.purpose: Sets up GL accounts that are allowed as overrides on A/R transactions, restricting overrides to an approved list.
scr_ar_setting_up_override_accounts.outcome: Overrides limited to sensible alternative accounts.
scr_ar_setting_up_override_accounts.rootCause: An open override lets users code revenue anywhere; an approved list keeps flexibility while preventing coding to balance sheet or expense accounts.
scr_ar_setting_up_override_accounts.ifSkipped: Overrides post revenue to inappropriate accounts.
redFlags: Override list including cash accounts

scr_ar_account_labels.purpose: Chapter on A/R account labels — the named mappings (e.g., 'Base Rent', 'CAM', 'Late Fee') that tie invoice lines to revenue GL accounts.
scr_ar_account_labels.outcome: A clean, controlled label list driving revenue coding.
scr_ar_account_labels.rootCause: Labels are the main control over revenue classification in A/R; a clean list keeps base rent, recoveries and other income separated as owners and ASC 842 disclosures require.
scr_ar_account_labels.ifSkipped: Revenue classification drifts and owner reports misstate categories.
redFlags: Labels that map to the same account under different names

scr_ar_account_labels_list.purpose: Lists A/R account labels with their mapped GL accounts and status, and is where new labels are added.
scr_ar_account_labels_list.outcome: A reviewable map of labels to revenue accounts.
scr_ar_account_labels_list.rootCause: Periodic review of the label list catches labels mapped to wrong accounts before they misclassify a month of billing.
scr_ar_account_labels_list.ifSkipped: Mis-mapped labels continue to misclassify revenue unnoticed.
redFlags: Active labels mapped to inactive accounts

scr_ar_viewing_and_editing_account_label.purpose: Views or edits an account label — its name, description and mapped GL account — affecting all future invoice lines using it.
scr_ar_viewing_and_editing_account_label.rootCause: Changing a label's account changes coding for every future invoice but not past ones; edits need approval and may require reclassifying history.
scr_ar_viewing_and_editing_account_label.ifSkipped: Wrong mappings persist; or edits made carelessly split history across accounts.
redFlags: Label account changed mid-year without reclass

scr_ar_finding_account_labels.purpose: Searches and filters the account label list by name, account or status to locate a specific label.
scr_ar_finding_account_labels.outcome: The correct label found quickly for review or use.
scr_ar_finding_account_labels.rootCause: Large companies accumulate many labels; searching avoids creating duplicates when the needed label already exists.
scr_ar_finding_account_labels.ifSkipped: Duplicate labels are created because existing ones were not found.
redFlags: Near-duplicate label names

scr_ar_deleting_an_account_label.purpose: Explains that labels used on transactions cannot be deleted and must instead be made inactive to stop further use.
scr_ar_deleting_an_account_label.outcome: Obsolete labels retired without breaking history.
scr_ar_deleting_an_account_label.rootCause: Deleting a used label would orphan historical invoice lines; inactivation preserves history while preventing new use.
scr_ar_deleting_an_account_label.ifSkipped: Obsolete labels remain selectable and continue to be used.
redFlags: Obsolete labels still active

scr_ar_exporting_the_account_label_list.purpose: Exports the account label list with mapped accounts for review, audit or documentation of revenue coding.
scr_ar_exporting_the_account_label_list.rootCause: Auditors and controllers review revenue coding controls; an exported label map is the evidence of how revenue is classified.
scr_ar_exporting_the_account_label_list.ifSkipped: Revenue coding controls cannot be evidenced.
redFlags: No periodic review of label map

scr_ar_printing_the_list_of_account_labe.purpose: Prints or exports the list of account labels for offline review or documentation packages.
scr_ar_printing_the_list_of_account_labe.outcome: A printable label list for review sign-off.
scr_ar_printing_the_list_of_account_labe.rootCause: Annual control reviews often require signed evidence that the label mapping was reviewed; a printed list provides it.
scr_ar_printing_the_list_of_account_labe.ifSkipped: There is no signed evidence that the revenue label mapping was reviewed this year.
redFlags: Review sign-off missing

scr_ar_account_label_information_page.purpose: The account label record page — label name, description, GL account, status and optional defaults such as tax or dimension values.
scr_ar_account_label_information_page.outcome: A complete label definition driving invoice line coding.
scr_ar_account_label_information_page.rootCause: Every invoice line using the label inherits this definition; completeness here prevents miscoding across all future billings.
scr_ar_account_label_information_page.ifSkipped: Incomplete labels cause inconsistent line coding.
redFlags: Labels missing descriptions

scr_ar_printing_the_account_label_detail.purpose: Prints the details of a single account label record for documentation or approval of a new or changed mapping.
scr_ar_printing_the_account_label_detail.outcome: Evidence of an individual label's configuration.
scr_ar_printing_the_account_label_detail.rootCause: New revenue labels should be approved by the controller; printing the record supports that approval evidence.
scr_ar_printing_the_account_label_detail.ifSkipped: New revenue labels go live with no documented controller approval.
redFlags: Labels created without approval evidence

scr_ar_exporting_the_account_label_detai.purpose: Exports an account label record (e.g., XML or PDF) for documentation, migration or integration purposes.
scr_ar_exporting_the_account_label_detai.outcome: Label configuration captured in a portable format.
scr_ar_exporting_the_account_label_detai.rootCause: During system migrations or integrations, exported label definitions ensure revenue mapping is replicated exactly.
scr_ar_exporting_the_account_label_detai.ifSkipped: Mapping must be rebuilt by hand in other systems.
redFlags: Mappings differing between systems

scr_ar_intercompany_bill_backs_2.purpose: Explains how bill-back templates automate intercompany charges — defining accounts on both sides so a bill-back creates matching invoice and bill.
scr_ar_intercompany_bill_backs_2.outcome: Consistent intercompany billing driven by templates.
scr_ar_intercompany_bill_backs_2.rootCause: Templates remove the chance of users picking different accounts on each side, which is what causes intercompany mismatches.
scr_ar_intercompany_bill_backs_2.ifSkipped: Intercompany entries use inconsistent accounts and do not mirror.
redFlags: Bill-backs created outside templates

scr_ar_bill_back_templates_list.purpose: Lists bill-back templates with their source and target accounts and status, and is where templates are added.
scr_ar_bill_back_templates_list.outcome: A reviewable set of intercompany charge templates.
scr_ar_bill_back_templates_list.rootCause: Periodic review of templates ensures intercompany charges still reflect current cost-sharing agreements between entities.
scr_ar_bill_back_templates_list.ifSkipped: Outdated templates continue charging entities under old agreements.
redFlags: Templates for entities no longer owned

scr_ar_editing_and_viewing_a_bill_back_t.purpose: Views or edits a bill-back template's invoice-side and bill-side GL accounts, description and entity settings when a cost-sharing agreement changes.
scr_ar_editing_and_viewing_a_bill_back_t.outcome: Template mapping corrected or updated for new agreements.
scr_ar_editing_and_viewing_a_bill_back_t.rootCause: Cost-sharing agreements change (new allocation bases, new entities); templates must be updated to reflect them.
scr_ar_editing_and_viewing_a_bill_back_t.ifSkipped: Bill-backs keep posting under an outdated cost-sharing mapping.
redFlags: Template edits without approval

scr_ar_deleting_a_bill_back_template.purpose: Deletes a bill-back template that is no longer used, typically after a cost-sharing arrangement ends or an entity is sold.
scr_ar_deleting_a_bill_back_template.rootCause: Leaving templates for sold entities lets users bill entities the company no longer manages.
scr_ar_deleting_a_bill_back_template.ifSkipped: Charges can still be billed to entities no longer in the portfolio.
redFlags: Deleting templates still referenced by open bill-backs

scr_ar_bill_back_template_information_pa.purpose: The bill-back template record page — name, description, invoice-side and bill-side accounts, and entity associations.
scr_ar_bill_back_template_information_pa.outcome: A complete definition of how an intercompany charge posts on both sides.
scr_ar_bill_back_template_information_pa.rootCause: The template is the single definition of both halves of the intercompany entry; completeness ensures the two sides always mirror.
scr_ar_bill_back_template_information_pa.ifSkipped: Incomplete templates create one-sided intercompany entries.
redFlags: Templates missing bill-side account

scr_ar_duplicating_a_bill_back_template.purpose: Duplicates an existing bill-back template to quickly create a similar one for another cost type or entity pair.
scr_ar_duplicating_a_bill_back_template.outcome: Faster setup of similar intercompany templates.
scr_ar_duplicating_a_bill_back_template.rootCause: Duplication speeds setup but copies accounts that may be wrong for the new cost type; each duplicate must be reviewed.
scr_ar_duplicating_a_bill_back_template.ifSkipped: Similar templates are built from scratch inconsistently.
redFlags: Duplicates left with source template accounts

scr_ar_overriding_the_g_l_account_in_a_r.purpose: Chapter on GL account overrides in A/R — enabling the feature, defining alternative accounts, permissions, per-customer alternatives and precedence.
scr_ar_overriding_the_g_l_account_in_a_r.outcome: Controlled flexibility in A/R revenue coding.
scr_ar_overriding_the_g_l_account_in_a_r.rootCause: Some customers or charges need non-default revenue accounts (e.g., affiliated tenant rent to a related-party revenue account for ASC 850 disclosure); overrides provide this in a controlled way.
scr_ar_overriding_the_g_l_account_in_a_r.ifSkipped: Exceptional coding is done by manual JEs outside the subledger.
redFlags: Related-party rent not separated

scr_ar_setting_up_g_l_account_override_w.purpose: The step-by-step workflow for setting up GL overrides — enable, define alternatives, grant permissions, assign per customer.
scr_ar_setting_up_g_l_account_override_w.outcome: Overrides configured completely and in order.
scr_ar_setting_up_g_l_account_override_w.rootCause: Skipping a step (e.g., permissions) either blocks legitimate overrides or leaves them open to everyone.
scr_ar_setting_up_g_l_account_override_w.ifSkipped: Overrides are either unusable or uncontrolled.
redFlags: Override enabled without permission setup

scr_ar_enabling_g_l_account_override.purpose: Turns on the GL account override feature in A/R configuration so transaction lines can use alternative accounts.
scr_ar_enabling_g_l_account_override.outcome: Override capability available for configured users.
scr_ar_enabling_g_l_account_override.rootCause: Overrides are off by default to protect coding integrity; enabling is a deliberate policy decision by the controller.
scr_ar_enabling_g_l_account_override.ifSkipped: Legitimate alternative coding cannot be performed in A/R.
redFlags: Enabled without controller approval

scr_ar_setting_up_an_alternative_g_l_acc.purpose: Defines the alternative GL accounts allowed as overrides — the whitelist users can choose from on A/R lines.
scr_ar_setting_up_an_alternative_g_l_acc.rootCause: A short, approved list is what stops overrides from becoming a route to misclassify revenue or hide credits in expense accounts.
scr_ar_setting_up_an_alternative_g_l_acc.ifSkipped: Users can override to any account including balance sheet accounts.
redFlags: Expense accounts on revenue override list

scr_ar_enabling_user_permissions_for_ove.purpose: Grants specific users or roles the permission to override default GL accounts on A/R invoice and adjustment lines.
scr_ar_enabling_user_permissions_for_ove.outcome: Only trusted users can apply overrides.
scr_ar_enabling_user_permissions_for_ove.rootCause: Limiting overrides to senior staff reduces misclassification risk and supports segregation of duties.
scr_ar_enabling_user_permissions_for_ove.ifSkipped: Anyone can override coding, weakening revenue controls.
redFlags: All users granted override rights

scr_ar_setting_an_alternative_g_l_accoun.purpose: Assigns an alternative GL account to a specific customer so its invoices automatically post to that account — for example an affiliate tenant's rent to related-party revenue.
scr_ar_setting_an_alternative_g_l_accoun.rootCause: Related-party and special-category customers must be tracked separately for disclosure; per-customer alternatives do this automatically every billing.
scr_ar_setting_an_alternative_g_l_accoun.ifSkipped: Related-party revenue mixes with third-party rent and disclosures are wrong.
redFlags: Affiliate tenants without alternative accounts

scr_ar_overriding_the_default_g_l_accoun.purpose: Overrides the default GL account on a specific A/R line at the time of entry, choosing from the permitted alternative list.
scr_ar_overriding_the_default_g_l_accoun.outcome: An individual line coded to the appropriate alternative account.
scr_ar_overriding_the_default_g_l_accoun.rootCause: One-off charges (insurance proceeds, legal settlements) need specific accounts; line-level override handles them without new labels.
scr_ar_overriding_the_default_g_l_accoun.ifSkipped: One-off income is coded to default accounts and misclassified.
redFlags: Overrides without explanation memo

scr_ar_order_of_precedence_in_a_transact.purpose: Explains which GL account wins when a transaction has several possible alternatives — line override, customer alternative, label default.
scr_ar_order_of_precedence_in_a_transact.outcome: Predictable coding when multiple rules apply.
scr_ar_order_of_precedence_in_a_transact.rootCause: Unexpected coding usually comes from precedence rules; understanding them lets reviewers explain and fix why a line hit a particular account.
scr_ar_order_of_precedence_in_a_transact.ifSkipped: Coding surprises cannot be explained or corrected at the source.
redFlags: Lines posting to unexpected accounts

scr_ar_a_r_terms.purpose: Chapter on configuring A/R terms — due dates, discounts and credit rules — consistently across entities.
scr_ar_a_r_terms.outcome: Consistent credit terms driving due dates and aging.
scr_ar_a_r_terms.rootCause: Terms determine when invoices become past due, which drives late fees, collections and the credit-loss reserve; inconsistent terms distort all three.
scr_ar_a_r_terms.ifSkipped: Aging and late-fee eligibility vary arbitrarily between properties.
redFlags: Different terms for identical lease structures

scr_ar_terms_overview.purpose: Explains A/R terms as the company's rules for extending credit — due-date calculation, discount percentage and window, and penalty linkage.
scr_ar_terms_overview.outcome: Users understand how terms drive due dates and discounts.
scr_ar_terms_overview.rootCause: Terms should mirror lease payment clauses (e.g., rent due the 1st, late after the 5th); understanding the link lets accountants set terms that match contracts.
scr_ar_terms_overview.ifSkipped: Terms diverge from lease clauses and late fees become unenforceable.
redFlags: Terms inconsistent with lease grace periods

scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_terms.purpose: Views the list of A/R terms defined for the company with due-date and discount rules.
scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_terms.outcome: A quick view of available terms before assigning them to customers.
scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_terms.rootCause: Reviewing existing terms before creating a new one avoids duplicate terms with slightly different rules.
redFlags: Several terms named 'Net 30' with different rules

scr_ar_a_r_terms_list.purpose: The A/R Terms list page — add new terms, edit existing ones and change status — controlling credit terms available to customers.
scr_ar_a_r_terms_list.outcome: A maintained, approved set of credit terms.
scr_ar_a_r_terms_list.rootCause: Terms are a credit policy control; a maintained list approved by the controller keeps site staff from granting unusual credit terms.
scr_ar_a_r_terms_list.ifSkipped: Unapproved generous terms extend credit risk and delay collections.
redFlags: Terms longer than Net 60 on rent
